Soft golden-hour light bathes the white spires, drifting fairy-motes glowing in the warm hazy air, the windows beginning to glow amber.
Cool blue moonlight washes the city, the windows glowing warm against it, a faint silver mist and floating motes hanging in the still air.
A rippling green aurora glows behind the spires, glowing pollen-light drifting through the cold clear air, the towers softly luminous.
Pearl-white misty dawn softens every edge, golden pollen-light drifting lazily upward, the high windows catching the first pale blush of morning.
Magical violet twilight settles between the spires, luminous sprites trailing slow arcs of light, the air thick with soft lavender haze.
Warm amber fae-lantern light pools along the bridges at dusk, motes swirling gently in the honeyed air, the stone glowing faintly beneath them.
Dappled green forest-light filters through the canopy above, glowing motes drifting like slow sparks, the leafy towers soft and luminous in the hush.
Rosy blossom-tinted dusk wraps the city in a warm blush, pale petals and tiny lights drifting together through the sweetly perfumed air.
A silver full-moon glow floods the open squares, thin white mist pooling at the roots, fae-lights hovering still in the breathless cold air.
Bioluminescent night glimmers across every surface, drifting blue-green lights rising slowly from the gardens, the dark air alive with soft pulsing radiance.
Soft pink alpenglow crowns the highest spires, rose-lit motes floating upward through the cool still air, the lower city fading into lavender shadow.
A gentle starlit dark settles over the city, glowing windows and drifting fae-lights studding the deep blue air like scattered embers.
A warm coral sunrise floods the eastern spires, gold motes catching the angled light, the whole city suspended in a rose-and-amber haze.
Deep indigo night with a thousand fae-lanterns swaying, their warm light scattering across the mist, motes drifting in slow golden spirals beneath them.
A soft teal twilight cools the air between the towers, bioluminescent motes rising from the river below, the bridges glowing faintly in the dusk.
Thick silver fog swallows the lower city, only the highest spires catching pale gold light, floating luminous specks drifting through the silent muffled air.
A warm copper late-afternoon haze drapes the arched walkways, lazy amber motes turning slowly in the slanted light, windows beginning to kindle from within.
Pale winterblue light and a sharp frost-haze, tiny crystalline motes catching the low sun and sparkling, the spires rimed with soft cold luminescence.
Soft green-gold light filters through enormous canopy leaves, the air below dim and warm, glowing moss-motes drifting on the slow circular breeze.
A deep rose twilight bleeds into navy above, fae-fire orbs floating between the spires, the last warm glow pooling in the carved stone below.
Warm firefly-gold night, hundreds of small lights drifting through the dark gardens and arched streets, the air soft and humming faintly with their glow.
A luminous white midsummer noon haze, the city almost overexposed in pale brilliance, slow white motes hanging weightless in the still breathless open air.
Stormy blue-grey light before rain, the city hushed and electric, glowing window-light and pale fae-motes the only warmth in the charged silver air.
A deep amber harvest-moon glow floods the plazas, long shadows stretching thin, drifting ember-motes rising from the lanterns into the warm smoky air.
Soft lilac pre-dawn quiet, the city still dark below and barely pink above, tiny luminous motes the only movement in the cool sleeping air.
